Rules video storyboard

Every beat of the video in order, in the guide and app look: the frame, when it lands, the voiceover line, and what moves. About 2:10 total. Sections 1–8 match video/SCRIPT.md.

1 · Cold open

0:00

(no voiceover)

White screen, a Clipper-card tap sound. The 41 neighborhood outlines draw in one after another.

0:05

“Two teams. Forty-one neighborhoods. One clock. This is Clipper Conquest.”

A few neighborhoods fill red and blue; the title slides in.

2 · The basic idea

0:10

“Clipper Conquest is played by two teams that race to conquer as many San Francisco neighborhoods as possible. Whichever team has more neighborhoods when the clock hits zero is the winner.”

Map resets to grey; the 41 counts up as neighborhoods ripple.

0:20

“Every one of the city's 41 neighborhoods has three unique challenges — get three antique arcade machines running at once, count the sea lions with a teammate, or just climb to Coit Tower. Complete them to conquer the neighborhood.”

Zoom to North Beach, which turns yellow; three challenge cards slide in one by one.

3 · Muni only

0:30

“You get around on Muni, and only Muni. Buses, Metro, streetcars, cable cars. No BART, no Caltrain, no cars, no bikes. And no running — speedwalk.”

Pull back; Muni lines draw in their real colors. The red team dot rides the F-line and the Powell–Mason cable car to North Beach. Checklist ticks in.

4 · Photo proof

0:45

“When you finish a challenge, take a photo — every completion needs one…”

Phone slides up on Get to Coit Tower; camera shutter click.

0:52

“…and log it in the app. The moment you log it is the moment it counts.”

A Coit Tower photo drops in; thumb taps Complete; it becomes ✓ 11:58.

5 · Conquering

1:05

“You can conquer a neighborhood by completing its challenges.”

Back on North Beach, empty timeline.

1:10

“Blue completes one. North Beach is Blue's — quickly.”

Row slides into the timeline; North Beach floods blue; badge 0–1.

1:15

“But be careful: the other team can steal a neighborhood by completing more of its challenges than you. Red completes one…”

Red row; badge ticks to 1–1; North Beach stays blue (Blue got there first — explained later).

1:18

“…and then another. Two beats one. Red steals North Beach.”

Third row; North Beach flips red with a quick wipe; highlight row "Red takes North Beach".

1:25

“Blue answers with a second. Two–two. So who holds it?”

Fourth row; North Beach fills with red/blue stripes and freezes.

6 · Ties and locks

1:30

“Ties go to whoever got there first. Red logged its second challenge at 11:58; Blue didn't get there until 12:30. Red keeps North Beach.”

Timeline slides in; a marker sweeps left to right; flag pops at 11:58.

1:42

“Complete all three and the neighborhood is locked — no one can steal it. But it might take a long time to finish all three.”

Cut to Hayes Valley: three checks, spaced out to feel slow; then the lock snaps shut with a clunk.

7 · Quick or locked

1:50

“So there's a choice. Complete one challenge and you conquer a neighborhood quickly — but you're vulnerable to a steal.”

Full map mid-game; cost badges pop on every Blue neighborhood; the dashed route draws.

1:58

“Red finds three that Blue held with a single challenge each, and steals them all in an hour.”

Red team dot runs the route; Western Addition, Japantown and the Marina flip red; tally ticks up.

8 · Close

2:05

“Whichever team has more neighborhoods when the clock hits zero wins. Every rule and every challenge is in the guide.”

Map fades; end card with the guide QR code.

Voice samples (Piper, local)
